name: AX30G Modulation Delay, measured 2026-09-13
notes: delay/feedback/high_damp/balance/dry maps carried over unchanged from models/ax30g-sdly.json (measured 2026-09-13); not independently re-derived for MODD in this pass, per the SDLY captures sharing the same delay/feedback/damp/balance hardware blocks.

modulation centring: unipolar ABOVE the nominal Dly Time, i.e. delay(t) = D + depth + depth*lfo(t) with lfo in [-1,1] (engine's existing render_modd default) -- delay never goes below the displayed Dly Time. Evidence: 20 per-click instantaneous-delay readings across all 5 Feedback-0 captures, minimum observed 200.06 ms against a 200 ms nominal, zero readings below 200 ms; if modulation were bipolar around 200 ms roughly half of 20 independent phase samples would fall below 200 ms (p ~ 1e-6 under that hypothesis). Mean elevation above 200 ms tracks the measured depth amplitude (ratio to depth_ms: 1.02, 0.55, 1.06, 0.78 for the four Speed>=1 captures respectively; noisy with only 4 clicks/capture but consistently positive, never negative).

depth map: linear through the origin, k = 0.133 ms/step (least-squares fit through 0 on (10,1.3365),(25,3.3365 @ Speed 1),(25,3.3233 @ Speed 5),(50,6.6482); the Speed-0.2 depth-25 reading (2.467 ms) excluded as unreliable per docs/findings.md -- the 4 s sine20 segment is too short for a ~5 s LFO period).
speed map: identity (Speed n = n Hz), confirmed again here (n=1 -> 0.997/0.996 Hz across 3 captures, n=5 -> 4.99 Hz); n=0.2 unreliable (reads 0.314 Hz, tone too short).

lfo shape: sin (crest 0.73-0.80 on the derivative track across the 4 reliable Feedback-0 captures, well under the 0.85 tri threshold); update_every 1 (audio-rate, not stepped: step_ratio 0.02-0.05 << 0.3 threshold in all 4).

in_loop: true. burst_pitch verdict on the Feedback-25/Bal-50/50 capture is in_loop (compounding_ratio 1.60 > 1.4 threshold); the Bal-25/25 capture's click-timing loop_position verdict is NOT used for this (README: click timing cannot separate in-loop from after-loop) and its LFO reading (11.96 Hz) is dry leakage into the pitch track, not a real LFO rate.

feedback at Feedback 25: measured 0.437 (Bal 25/25) and 0.462 (Bal 50/50) by click peaks, both a bit below the SDLY table's 0.5 -- attributed to modulation smearing the repeat's cross-correlation peak (chorus-like broadening lowers the apparent peak amplitude versus a stationary click); the SDLY table value (0.5) is kept as the model's law rather than a MODD-specific refit, since the peaks-based numbers here are a known underestimate.
read interpolation: set by null-testing the Depth-50/Speed-1/Feedback-0 capture, see docs/modd-model-2026-09-13.md.
High Damp is 0 in every available capture, so damp.position and the pole_linear map's carried-over constants are UNTESTED for MODD (see open questions).
sample_rate 39057.3 is the same measured device clock as the SDLY model, used only for nulling against these captures; the plugin runs at 39062.5. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-16, see the dated note below.

2026-09-16: sample_rate -> 39063.829787 (effective 153/188 of 48 kHz), maps.delay gained offset_samples: 2, matching the SDLY model's adopted clock/delay-length law (docs/sdly-clock-2026-09-16.md, 'Adopted 2026-09-16'). MODD trajectory (tests/modd_trajectory.py, which absorbs a static delay offset through its per-capture phase fit and so cannot itself discriminate the law) confirmed not worse at the new rate/offset: Speed 1/Depth 25 rms 0.2175 -> 0.2178, Speed 5/Depth 50 rms 0.0781 -> 0.0782 device-samples, both at offset 0 and offset 2 identically (as expected -- the trajectory test cannot see a constant offset). No MODD capture nulls the delay length directly, so this change rides on the SDLY law rather than an independent MODD fit.

2026-09-13 16:15, long-tone captures (capture/signalset-lfo.wav, layout-lfo.json): LFO rate = 0.9984 n - 0.0018 Hz (0.20/1.00/5.00/9.50 -> 0.1979/0.9965/4.9897/9.4812 measured at the 39057.3 clock); waveform sine within 4 % of swing, no control-rate lines; sweep 10 samples p-p per Depth step (6.4 ms amplitude at 50); balance tables from the 11-point SDLY series; High Damp on the line input as measured on SDLY

2026-09-13 evening, LFO waveform replaced with the unit's own measured shape (docs/modd-lfo-table-2026-09-13.md): 256-point table extracted by synchronous averaging of the bandpass(700-1300 Hz)+Hilbert instantaneous-frequency delay trajectory on the Speed-1/Depth-25 long-tone capture (best-fit rate 0.996634 Hz), cross-checked on Speed-5/Depth-50 (best-fit rate 4.989680 Hz; normalised shapes agree to 0.00127 rms over [0,1]); stored table is the average of the two normalised, phase-rolled (min at index 0) cycles. 3rd/5th harmonic -24.9/-34.4 dB relative to the fundamental on both captures; rms deviation from a best-fit sine 5.69 device-samples (Depth 25) / 11.40 device-samples (Depth 50), i.e. about 2.2% rms / 6.6% peak of the p-p swing -- consistent with the ~4% figure that was already flagged as enough to explain a near-0 dB null of an ideal-sine model. maps.depth.out_max updated 6.4 -> 6.5247 ms from the measured p-p (254.95 device-samples at Depth 25 = 10.198 samples/Depth-unit, 509.45 at Depth 50 = 10.189 samples/Depth-unit, average 10.1935 vs the prior spec's 10.0).

2026-09-14 14:05, LFO set at Speeds 0.5/2/3/7 (captures ..._Speed-{0.5,2,3,7}_Depth-25_..._SET-lfo): measured rates 0.495995 / 1.993121 / 2.991968 / 6.985249 Hz at the 39057.3 clock (tests/modd_trajectory.py period fit), added to maps.speed; the table is now 9 points 0..9.5. The 'Speed 0.02' capture of the same session runs at 0.198015 Hz, the same as the Speed-0.2 capture, so it is not a new point (either the unit's minimum is 0.2 or the setting was 0.20; unresolved).

2026-09-14 15:10, slow speeds on a 120 s tone (captures ..._Speed-{0.02,0.1,0.18}_..._SET-lfo, capture/signalset-lfo120.wav): rates from corner-to-corner periods 0.01863 / 0.09779 / 0.17696 Hz (53.686 / 10.226 / 5.651 s, identical from minima and maxima). Every measured rate is an integer multiple of 39062.5/2^24 = 0.0023283 Hz to within 0.2 (k = 8, 42, 76, 85, 213, 428, 856, 1285, 2143, 3000, 4072 for the 11 display values), i.e. a 24-bit phase accumulator at the device rate; k is about 428.6 n above 1 Hz and falls short at the slow end (400 n at 0.02), so the table, not a formula, remains the law. The earlier 30 s-tone '0.02' capture (0.198 Hz) had been dialled to 0.2.
